correctness.rationale: The two-target-point argument localizes each target-level preimage to one source antichain. The upward bounded-morphism back property, applied to an alternative point of a higher target antichain, rules out distinct target levels sharing the same source level. These give an increasing bijection of level indices and force equal heights and levelwise surjections. Conversely independently surjective level maps meet HP and BP. Standard Stirling counts then follow, and splitting a singleton target level gives a valid sharp counterexample. A separate exhaustive verifier checks all 181 designated small configurations and the singleton boundary. Finite checks are corroboration only.

value.rationale: The result completely classifies the bounded-morphic-image preorder for finite layered Kripke frames with all target levels nontrivial and gives an exact labelled enumeration of all quotients. This provides a tractable structural island inside the generally NP-hard finite-poset SPMorph problem. The singleton-target construction isolates precisely where height rigidity fails, making the result a motivated sharp classification rather than a routine numerical instance.
